subject.title: Maintainer default quota is a shared policy pool; no per-user budgets or self-service keys

question: What canonical subject should own monthly spend, and may a verified non-admin Access user mint a durable credential only for that subject and their current policy binding?
rationale: This choice changes durable accounting identity, revocation behavior, and who may create bearer credentials; source inspection cannot infer the intended security boundary.

options.title: Human principal plus service policy
options.body: Use verified principal identity for rule-assigned human sessions and their self-issued keys, while retaining policy-scoped pools for explicitly service-owned credentials.

options.title: Generated policy per principal
options.body: Materialize a managed policy for every assigned user so existing policy-ledger and administrator issuance semantics remain structurally unchanged.

options.title: Keep shared administrator pools
options.body: Retain policy-wide budgets and administrator-only issuance, documenting maintainer access as a collective quota rather than an individual allowance.

recommendation.title: Human principal plus service policy
recommendation.body: Use verified principal identity for rule-assigned human sessions and their self-issued keys, while retaining policy-scoped pools for explicitly service-owned credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across Access identity, usage accounting, budget behavior, and the affected admin surfaces.
